lead_story.topic: Giannis Antetokounmpo debuts for Heat in blowout loss to Timberwolves — new Big Three gets blown out 131-106, LaMelo Ball dominates
lead_story.headline: Giannis' Heat debut: a 25-point blowout loss
lead_story.research_notes: CONTINUING [Day 2]: Giannis Antetokounmpo debuts for Miami Heat in 131-106 blowout loss to Timberwolves. Giannis: 10 PTS, 8 REB, 5 AST, 3-12 FG per HaterReport — underwhelming debut for superstar who was supposed to lift Heat to contention. LaMelo Ball: 29 PTS, 7 REB, 10 AST per StatMuse — screaming after Giannis missed FT per HaterReport. Anthony Edwards cussing out Heat bench all game per HaterReport — 'A player on they bench was talkin trash... talkin pretty crazy… when I started talkin to him he didn't really have too much to say… if you gonna talk sh*t keep talkin sh*t. Don't get quiet' per HaterReport. Ant and Melo's Timberwolves dominant opening night. Heat's new Big Three (Giannis, Kawhi Leonard, teammates) gets demolished by 25 in opener. CBS Sports already ran 'Giannis gets nothing from new Heat teammates; Steph Curry could be in for a long year' headline per raw content. The contrast: Giannis came to Miami to win now, first game is 25-point blowout at home. How does this compare to other superstar debut disasters? LeBron's first Heat game (lost opener but kept it close), Kawhi's Clippers debut (won big), Harden's Nets debut (good). This might be worst debut for championship-level expectation in years. The viral moment: LaMelo screaming after Giannis missed FT — that's the image that will define this night. Miami's title hopes already in question after one game.
lead_story.gif_concept: Quiet resignation as the season begins — the look when you realize this might be a long year

beats.angle: Giannis' debut statline: 10-8-5 on 3-12 shooting in 25-point home loss
beats.landing: The reader sees the gap between expectation (championship contender) and reality (blown out at home)

beats.angle: LaMelo Ball and Anthony Edwards dominating — Melo screaming after Giannis missed FT, Ant cussing out Heat bench all game
beats.landing: The Timberwolves' young stars embarrassed Miami's new superteam on opening night

beats.angle: How does this debut compare to other superstar first games with championship expectations?
beats.landing: This might be the worst debut for a title-favorite superstar in years — LeBron's Heat debut was a loss but competitive, Kawhi's Clippers debut was a statement win, Harden's Nets debut was strong. Giannis got blown out by 25 at home.

supporting_stories.topic: Blazers demolish Suns 124-83 — Dame 25 points, Ja Morant 14 in debut, Portland's new Big 3 arrives
supporting_stories.headline: Blazers destroy Suns: Dame-Ja era begins
supporting_stories.research_notes: Portland demolishes Phoenix 124-83 per ground truth — 41-point blowout. Damian Lillard in return: 25 PTS, 6 AST, 7-12 FG, 6-10 3PT, +23 in only 24 MIN per StatMuse. Ja Morant in Blazers debut: 14 PTS, 5 REB, 8 AST, 3 STL, 6-8 FG, +33 per StatMuse — third-highest single-game +/- of his career per StatMuse. Deni Avdija: 18 PTS, 10 REB per ClutchPoints. Suns scored 83 points total — BarstoolBigCat: 'Thanks for coming out, Suns.' This was supposed to be a competitive Western Conference matchup. Instead Portland's new Big 3 (Dame back home, Ja, Deni) announced themselves with a 41-point demolition. Dame barely played (24 min) because the game was over. How does this compare to other 'homecoming' games? Dame left Portland for Milwaukee in trade, now he's back and immediately blowing out opponents. The Suns are supposed to be good — Kevin Durant, Devin Booker — and they scored 83 points. What does this say about Portland's defensive identity this year?

supporting_stories.topic: Ty Jerome drops career-high 45 points vs Jazz — first Grizzly in franchise history with 45/5/5 on 65+ FG%
supporting_stories.headline: Ty Jerome's 45-point explosion

tweets.text: Ty Jerome vs Utah: 45 PTS (career-high) 7 REB 6 AST 17-25 FG The first Grizzly in franchise history with a 45/5/5 game on 65+ FG%.

supporting_stories.research_notes: Memphis beat Utah 123-103. Ty Jerome: 45 PTS (career-high), 7 REB, 6 AST, 17-25 FG per StatMuse — first Grizzly in franchise history with a 45/5/5 game on 65+ FG% per StatMuse. Jerome is a journeyman guard who has bounced around the league (Suns, Thunder, Rockets, Warriors, Cavaliers per basketball-reference). This is his 7th NBA season. Career high coming into tonight was probably low 20s. To drop 45 on 68% shooting is absurd. How does this compare to other unexpected explosions by role players? Corey Brewer 51 points, Terrence Ross 51 points, Tony Delk 53 points — all journeymen who had one nuclear night. Where does Jerome rank in 'out of nowhere' career-high performances? This is the kind of game that makes you wonder if he's been underutilized his whole career or if it's just a one-off. Memphis won by 20, so this wasn't garbage time — Jerome was the reason they pulled away.
supporting_stories.gif_concept: Bewildered by a bizarre moment — what just happened?

beats.angle: Ty Jerome's 45-point, 17-for-25 masterpiece — first Grizzly ever with 45/5/5 on 65+ shooting
beats.landing: A journeyman guard who's bounced around the league just made franchise history in a way no one saw coming

beats.angle: How does this compare to other 'out of nowhere' career-high explosions by role players?
beats.landing: Jerome joins the pantheon of journeymen who dropped 50+ (or in this case 45+) in one random game — Corey Brewer, Terrence Ross, Tony Delk all did it, and we're still talking about those games years later
